notes: Fiscal year ended 30 June 2026 (FY26, matching data.js 'Jun 2026'). Source is the 'FY26 Annual Report and Appendix 4E' lodged on the ASX on 20 August 2026 (ASX announcements host). Fortescue reports in US dollars; values converted exactly from US$m. OWNERSHIP: the leader's figure is Dr Andrew Forrest's own Form 604 substantial holder notice lodged on 11 November 2026: on 9 November 2026 his relevant interest became 1,090,033,238 shares, 35.40% of voting power (he acquired a relevant interest in 8,668,238 shares under a power of attorney for his mother, Judith Street, and ceased to hold a relevant interest in 50,000,000 shares held by Coaxial Ventures Pty Ltd, a Nicola Forrest entity; Appendix 3Y of 9 November 2026 gives the same 1,090,033,238). The FY26 annual report (shareholder information at 17 August 2026) still listed the joint group of Tattarang Pty Ltd, Minderoo Foundation Limited, Nicola Margaret Forrest and John Andrew Henry Forrest at 1,131,365,000 shares (36.74% of issued capital), based on the June 2023 notice, and its directors' report gives the same 1,131,365,000 as his relevant interest (s205G). Nicola Forrest's own notice of the same date keeps 1,131,331,637 (36.74%) as her relevant interest, so the two Forrest figures overlap and are not added. The relevant interest includes shares held by Tattarang and by the Minderoo Foundation (a charitable foundation), which the filings do not split. HOLDERS: from the annual report's substantial holders list. That list also gave BlackRock Group at 154,473,810 shares (5.01%), but BlackRock has since crossed 5% several times; its latest notice on the ASX (Form 605, lodged 20 October 2026, https://announcements.asx.com.au/asxpdf/20261020/pdf/075j7djyjqdpt2.pdf, a scanned image read visually) says it ceased to be a substantial holder on 16 October 2026, a day after becoming one again with 4.90% of ordinary shares plus 0.11% through ADRs. So BlackRock is not listed. Nominee and custodian accounts (Citicorp Nominees 35.39%, HSBC Custody Nominees 17.55%, J P Morgan Nominees 7.57%) are not beneficial owners and are excluded; Valin Investments (Singapore) register entries are taken to sit within Hunan Valin's substantial holding. relation 'founder': the board section describes him as 'Executive Chairman and Founder of Fortescue'. BUYBACKS: 0. No shares were bought back under the buy-back program in FY26; the US$157m 'Purchase of shares by employee share trust' buys shares for employee awards and is excluded under the schema rule. DIVIDENDS: US$2,529m (final FY25 A$0.60 and interim FY26 A$0.62 per share, fully franked). STOCK COMP: US$195m share-based payment expense.

No newer edition found (checked 2026-11-24): the FY26 sustainability site's report library still lists the FY2025 CbC report, and the FY26 Sustainability Report refers only to 'our latest available public Country-by-Country Report'. Only jurisdictions with employees or cash tax paid are listed; dashes (nil) are omitted, not recorded as 0. 6 employees working where Fortescue has no local entity ('Other countries') are not in the rows. The large U.K. headcount (1,182) is Fortescue's U.K. operations, which the report shows with losses. Cash tax excludes Western Australian state royalties; no royalty breakdown by jurisdiction was recorded. No state or regional data. Sites are re-read from the FY26 annual report (lodged with the ASX with the Appendix 4E on Aug 20, 2026): the Pilbara (Western Australia) mines, Iron Bridge, Herb Elliott Port and the Belinga project in Gabon; the mines connect to Port Hedland via 760km of rail. The FY26 report does not restate the headquarters address, so the Perth HQ (the Fortescue Hive at 256 St Georges Terrace) is still cited from the FY25 annual report.
